question: Lines: A line is made up of a infinite number of points and it has only length i.e., it does not has any thickness (or width). A line is endless so, it can be extended in both directions.
options: (i) Intersecting Lines: If two or more lines intersect each other, then they are called intersecting lines. In the figure AB and CD are intersecting lines.
(ii) Concurrent Lines : If three or more lines pass through a point, then they are called concurrent lines and the point through which these all lines pass is called point of concurrent.

(iii) Parallel Lines : Two straight lines are parallel if they lie in the same plane and do not intersect even if they produced infinitely. Perpendicular distances between two parallel lines are always same at all places.
(iv) Perpendicular Lines : If two lines intersect at right angles, then two lines are called perpendicular lines. In the following figure AB and CD are perpendicular lines.
explanation: Correct Answer: Option A | ((i) Intersecting Lines: If two or more lines intersect each other, then they are called intersecting lines. In the figure AB and CD are intersecting lines.)
